hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I'm inquiring about my child. I have one child, Alex, who's 10 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I understand you're inquiring about Child Benefit for your 10-year-old child, Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex? That is, do you live with Alex and are you responsible for their care and upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do help out with some money for their upkeep - I contribute towards things like clothes and pocket money.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's important information.

**Does Alex live with someone else who is responsible for their day-to-day care (such as the other parent, a relative, or a guardian)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with their other parent who looks after them day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

**Just to confirm: Are you and Alex both living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we're both in the UK. I live in Manchester, and Alex lives with their other parent here in the UK as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 10 years old and living in the UK
- Alex lives with their other parent who is responsible for their day-to-day care
- You contribute financially but Alex doesn't live with you and you're not responsible for their day-to-day care

The key rule for Child Benefit is that it's paid to the person who is **responsible for the child**, which generally means the person the child lives with and who looks after them on a day-to-day basis. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. If more than one person is responsible for the same child, only one of them can receive the benefit - usually the person with main responsibility.

Since Alex lives with their other parent who has day-to-day care responsibility, that parent would be the eligible person to claim Child Benefit for Alex, not you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on your circumstances, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 

Child Benefit can only be claimed by the person who is responsible for the child - this means the person the child lives with and who is responsible for their day-to-day care. Since Alex lives with their other parent who looks after them day-to-day, that parent would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

While it's great that you contribute financially to Alex's upkeep, this doesn't make you eligible for Child Benefit when another person has the main caring responsibility and Alex lives with them.

If you have any other questions about this decision, please feel free to ask.
